# Owned DEB inputs

`scripts/generate-deb-fixtures.py --ar-reference <pinned-bsdtar> [--check]` creates these packages from project-owned metadata and byte patterns. They are archive fixtures, never installed. The control TAR contains a `.` root, a fixed Deb822 `control` file and harmless `postinst` text that is never executed. The data TAR contains a `.` root, `usr/share/xdzip`, `hello.txt` with `abracadabra abracadabra\n` repeated six times, UTF-8 `资料.txt` containing `owned UTF-8 content\n`, and an empty file. Names, ownership, permissions and timestamps are fixed by the generator.

The 24 `control-*-data-*.deb` inputs cover four control profiles (none, GZIP, XZ, Zstandard) and six data profiles (also BZip2 and LZMA Alone). `extensions.deb` adds optional ar name terminators, underscore-prefixed intervening members, an extra trailing member and a compatible minor version with an additional line. `duplicates.deb` adds a second physical `hello.txt` with `second physical record\n`. Every package is independently listed and its raw members extracted and byte-compared with libarchive's `bsdtar` 3.8.9; Python 3.15.1 independently decompresses each inner member and compares its original TAR bytes.

The pinned test-only `bsdtar.exe` has SHA-256 `a3ac62fd4cdf619a7c53f71ca3fe5fb42f72020975670ff29afe3603f6416a8e` and reports libarchive 3.8.9, liblzma 5.8.3 and libzstd 1.5.7. It remains under local `build/toolchain/references/libarchive-3.8.9/`. No reference implementation code, user packages, installation result or generated execution report is stored here. The envelope contract follows [deb(5)](https://manpages.debian.org/unstable/dpkg-dev/deb.5.en.html) and [ar(5)](https://man.netbsd.org/ar.5).
